**Referee Report**

**Paper:** Spectrally Unusual Sources at Scale… (Houston Golden, submitted to Phys. Rev. D)

**Overall assessment:** The manuscript presents an unusually large anomaly catalog generated by a deterministic autoencoder pipeline applied to seven surveys. While the engineering effort is substantial, the paper contains multiple load-bearing statistical claims, an over-long format, and several places where the abstract or headline numbers are not fully supported by the displayed evidence or require stronger qualification. I would not accept in present form.

**ESSENTIAL findings (must be fixed for further consideration)**

P3-E1 (Abstract, p. 1; §V, p. 17)  
The abstract states “the central 9.4 % improvement” in the Fisher forecast for \(f_{\rm NL}\). The body (§V, Fig. 9, Table VIII) shows this 9.4 % figure is obtained only after inserting the empirically measured bias \(\alpha_{\rm jk}=0.19\pm0.65\) and is explicitly labeled “noise-driven… not a detection.” The abstract sentence is therefore stronger than the calibrated body statement.  
**Fix:** Remove the 9.4 % figure from the abstract or add the explicit qualifier “under the measured bias; consistent with zero improvement at \(<1\sigma\)”.

P3-E2 (Abstract, p. 1; §IV A, p. 13)  
Abstract advertises “a Native-Trained Novelty Fraction from 37.3 Million Sources.” The only quantitative novelty fraction given (17.8 % Wilson interval) is computed on the top-1 000 DESI objects alone. No equivalent fraction is computed or quoted for the full 378 k catalog or the other six surveys.  
**Fix:** Either compute and report a catalog-wide novelty fraction with the same methodology or excise the phrase from the abstract.

P3-E3 (§II B, p. 4; Eq. 2)  
The anomaly score \(S\) is defined with survey-specific \(\mu_{\rm val},\sigma_{\rm val}\) taken from each survey’s own 20 % validation split. The text repeatedly juxtaposes \(S>5\) thresholds across surveys without the explicit statement that the numerical values are not directly comparable. This violates the journal’s requirement for side-by-side \(\sigma\)-like quantities.  
**Fix:** Add the sentence “Because each \(S\) is standardized to its own validation distribution, numerical values of \(S\) are not directly comparable across surveys” at every location where multiple surveys’ \(S\) cuts are listed together (Table I, §III, §IV).

P3-E4 (§V, p. 17; Fig. 9)  
The multi-tracer Fisher improvement is reported as 6.1 % (central value) while the single-tracer baseline already incorporates the measured bias. The paper never states the effect size of the improvement relative to the shot-noise floor or the change in the \(1\sigma\) envelope width.  
**Fix:** Supply the fractional change in the \(1\sigma\) half-width and the corresponding \(\Delta\chi^2\) or state that the improvement lies inside the prior uncertainty.

**MAJOR findings**

P3-M1 (Length)  
29 pages for a catalog-plus-method paper exceeds typical PRD limits for this class of contribution. The cosmological section (§V) is only ~2 pages yet drives the abstract; the per-survey sections are largely repetitive.  
**Fix:** Reduce to ≤18 pages or justify the length with a clear statement of what new methodological ground is broken beyond prior single-survey autoencoder papers.

P3-M2 (§IV A, p. 13)  
The 17.8 % “genuine novelty fraction” is derived from a 5-arcsec SIMBAD cross-match on only the top-1 000 DESI objects. The paper acknowledges that SIMBAD is incomplete but does not propagate the incompleteness into the quoted Wilson interval.  
**Fix:** Provide a quantitative estimate of the false-novelty rate induced by SIMBAD incompleteness or re-label the 17.8 % figure as an upper limit.

P3-M3 (Fig. 3, p. 9; §III C)  
The right-hand panel shows the SDSS native-retrain score distribution extending to \(S\sim10^{11}\). No explanation is given for the 11-order-of-magnitude dynamic range or whether these extreme scores are dominated by a handful of pathological spectra.  
**Fix:** Add a robustness test removing the top 0.1 % of scores and re-computing all downstream statistics.

P3-M4 (§II D, p. 5)  
The Path-C “six-step validation protocol” is presented as the core methodological advance, yet the only quantitative cross-validation metric supplied is a 5-fold Jaccard of 0.862 on DESI. No equivalent metric is shown for the other six surveys after native retraining.  
**Fix:** Report the full set of Jaccard / OOD / injection-recovery numbers for every native retrain or state that only DESI was subjected to the complete protocol.

**MINOR findings**

P3-m1 (p. 1) “Dated: June 2026” — future date in a submitted manuscript.  
P3-m2 (Table I, footnote ¶) The 200 Planck patches are retained in the headline count but contribute zero objects to every science analysis; the table mixes two different selection functions without a separate column.  
P3-m3 (Fig. 2, p. 6) Mollweide map uses the initial cross-transfer baseline (319 k) rather than the final Path-C catalog; caption does not state this.

**NITs**  
- Inconsistent use of “Path-C” vs “native-retrain” terminology in figure captions.  
- Several figure axes lack explicit units (e.g., Fig. 3 right-hand panel).  
- Duplicate phrasing “the the” on p. 4, col. 2.

**Summary recommendation**  
**MAJOR REVISIONS**

The manuscript contains an impressive data volume but fails multiple PRD standards on statistical comparability, abstract–body consistency, and length. The cosmological claim is already hedged in the body yet still overstated in the abstract; the novelty fraction is reported only on a tiny, high-score subsample; and the methodological novelty is not demonstrated with uniform metrics across all seven surveys. A substantially shortened revision that (i) aligns every headline number with the most conservative body statement, (ii) supplies the missing cross-survey validation statistics, and (iii) removes or clearly caveats the 9.4 % and 17.8 % figures would be required before further review.
